samuel1.10.p1.b1.text: Then Samuel took a flask of oil, poured it on Saul’s head, kissed him, and said,

samuel1.10.p1.b2.text: “Has not the LORD anointed you ruler over His inheritance?

samuel1.10.p2.b1.text: When you leave me today, you will find two men at Rachel’s tomb in Zelzah on the border of Benjamin.

samuel1.10.p2.b2.text: ‘The donkeys you seek have been found, and now your father has stopped worrying about the donkeys and started worrying about you …’

samuel1.10.p2.b3.text: … until you come to the Oak of Tabor. Three men going up to God at Bethel will meet you there, one carrying three young goats, another carrying three loaves of bread, and another carrying a skin of wine.

samuel1.10.p2.b4.text: They will greet you and give you two loaves of bread, which you will accept from their hands.

samuel1.10.p3.b1.text: After that you will come to Gibeah of God … you will meet a group of prophets coming down from the high place, preceded by harps, tambourines, flutes, and lyres, and they will be prophesying.

samuel1.10.p3.b2.text: Then the Spirit of the LORD will rush upon you, and you will prophesy with them; and you will be transformed into a different person.

samuel1.10.p3.b3.text: And you shall go before me to Gilgal … Wait seven days until I come to you and show you what you are to do.”

samuel1.10.p3.b4.text: As Saul turned to leave Samuel, God changed Saul’s heart …

samuel1.10.p4.b1.text: When Saul and his servant arrived at Gibeah, a group of prophets met him. Then the Spirit of God rushed upon him, and he prophesied along with them.

samuel1.10.p4.b2.text: “What has happened to the son of Kish? Is Saul also among the prophets?”

samuel1.10.p4.b4.text: So the saying became a proverb: “Is Saul also among the prophets?”

samuel1.10.p5.b3.text: “He assured us that the donkeys had been found.”

samuel1.10.p5.b4.text: But Saul did not tell his uncle what Samuel had said about the kingship.

samuel1.10.p6.b1.text: After this, Samuel summoned the people to the LORD at Mizpah

samuel1.10.p6.b2.text: But today you have rejected your God, who saves you from all your troubles and afflictions, and you have said to Him, ‘No, set a king over us.’ …

samuel1.10.p6.b3.text: Thus Samuel had all the tribes of Israel come forward, and the tribe of Benjamin was selected.

samuel1.10.p6.b4.text: … Finally, Saul son of Kish was selected. But when they looked for him, they could not find him …

samuel1.10.p7.b1.text: So again they inquired of the LORD, “Has the man come here yet?”

samuel1.10.p7.b2.text: “Behold, he has hidden himself among the baggage.”

samuel1.10.p7.b3.text: “Do you see the one the LORD has chosen? There is no one like him among all the people.”

samuel1.10.p8.b1.text: Then Samuel explained to the people the rights of kingship. He wrote them on a scroll and laid it up before the LORD. And Samuel sent all the people away, each to his own home.

samuel1.10.p8.b2.text: Saul also went to his home in Gibeah, and the men of valor whose hearts God had touched went with him.

samuel1.10.p8.b4.text: … So they despised him and brought him no gifts; but Saul remained silent about it.
